newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares held gains achieved by noon to close up on Tuesday as Wall Street opened firmer, dealers said.
In the wake of the Dow's 250-point plunge last Friday, dealers said all eyes had been fixed on that market and relief at its stronger start encouraged local stocks.
"There was a little hop up to close. It really has been waiting for Wall Street and because it was slightly positive, stocks picked up slightly," said James Scott of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Although the local market remained nervous, waiting to see if Wall Street held or came off in continued correction, underlying demand was still there, dealers said.
Trade throughout the day had been cautious ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's speech later which would offer Wall Street further direction.
By 1425 GMT the Dow Jones Industrial index had retreated from opening levels to just up 11.61 points at 7,814.9.
Little other direction was offered the local market and South African shares were awaiting a raft of local economic data to point the way, dealers said.
"They're watching the FOMC and in the absence of leading economic indicators ourselves, we'll pretty much track Wall Street," Scott said.
Overall volumes, like Monday, were moderate with 679.7 million rand traded.
Advancing issues led decliners 231 to 143 with another 134 stocks traded but finishing unchanged.
South African computer firm IBM featured ahead of its interim results due later. The share closed 92 cents up at 870 cents in volume of 115,200 shares.
Some dealers were expecting results to be better, while others said results could disappoint, but that the outlook for company may be promising.
Good year results, announced on Monday, fuelled shares in South African firm Ingwe Coal Corp Ltd on Tuesday. Ingwe closed 20 cents up at 24.25 rand in a traded volume of 245,200 shares.
Shares in South African electronics to information technology firm Siltek Ltd also soared after the firm raised headline earnings for the year.
Siltek announced results on Monday showing headline earnings per share up to 202.53 cents from 173.96 cents previously.
The share closed 200 cents stronger at 25 rand in a volume of 419,100 shares traded.

Industrial shares finished 37.4 points up at 9,086.4 points, all-shares were carried 35.9 points to 7,397.2 points and golds were up 0.9 points to 1,017.6 points. South African industrial share futures started slightly firmer after Wall Street's overnight firmer finish, but by late trade they had slipped to hug settlement levels.
Gold share futures drifted lower throughout the day on a dull bullion price.
The near-term all share futures contract was last at 6,464/503 from 6,462, industrials were at 8,466/71 from 8,460 and golds at 726/54 from 740.
